questions.question: What is the 'sea of electrons' in metallic bonding?
options: Electrons floating on the surface of metals
Delocalized electrons that move freely throughout the metal
Electrons that are shared between two atoms
Electrons in the outer shell of metal atoms
questions.explanation: The 'sea of electrons' refers to delocalized electrons that are free to move throughout the entire metal structure, not attached to any specific atom.

questions.question: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?
options: They have delocalized electrons that can carry charge
They have a regular lattice structure
questions.explanation: Delocalized electrons in metals are free to move and can carry electrical charge throughout the metal, making metals good conductors.

questions.question: Which property of metals is explained by the delocalized electrons reflecting light?
questions.explanation: The metallic luster (shiny appearance) is caused by delocalized electrons reflecting light from the metal surface.

questions.question: Why are metals malleable?
options: The electron sea maintains bonding when layers slide
questions.explanation: When metal layers slide, the delocalized electrons move with them, maintaining the metallic bonding. This allows metals to be hammered into shape.

questions.question: Which metal would have stronger metallic bonding: Na or Mg?
options: Na - it has a larger atomic radius
Mg - it has 2 delocalized electrons per atom
Na - it has lower ionization energy
questions.explanation: Mg has 2 delocalized electrons per atom (compared to 1 for Na) and Mg²⁺ ions have higher charge than Na⁺, resulting in stronger metallic bonding.

questions.question: What is the main difference between metallic and ionic bonding?
options: Metallic bonding involves electron transfer, ionic involves sharing
Metallic bonding has delocalized electrons, ionic has fixed ions
questions.explanation: In metallic bonding, electrons are delocalized (free to move). In ionic bonding, electrons have been transferred and ions are fixed in the lattice.

questions.question: Why does magnesium (Mg) have a higher melting point than sodium (Na)?
options: Mg has more delocalized electrons and higher ion charge
questions.explanation: Mg has 2 delocalized electrons per atom and Mg²⁺ ions, creating stronger electrostatic attraction than Na with only 1 delocalized electron and Na⁺ ions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of metals?
questions.explanation: Metals are malleable, not brittle. Brittleness is a property of ionic compounds - when layers slide, like charges repel and the crystal breaks.

questions.question: What holds the metal ions together in a metallic lattice?
options: Electrostatic attraction to the sea of delocalized electrons
questions.explanation: Metal cations are held together by their electrostatic attraction to the delocalized electrons that surround them in the metallic lattice.

questions.question: A substance conducts electricity in both solid and molten states. What type of bonding does it have?
questions.explanation: Only metallic substances conduct electricity in both solid and molten states. Ionic compounds only conduct when molten or dissolved (ions free to move).
